baseline.name: Count and forward-fill formatted output
baseline.approach: Count retained characters, compute the first group length, then fill an exact-sized output buffer.
baseline.space: O(1) auxiliary state plus O(n) output

archived.name: Count and backward-fill output
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary state plus O(n) output

why: Backward grouping makes the short leading group fall out naturally, but it does not reduce the two-pass linear work versus a forward fill.
quantitative_comparison: Both scan n source characters for counting and up to n again for formatting, with one sized output allocation. No asymptotic or measured runtime improvement is established.
tradeoffs: Requires k>0, ASCII case mapping and bounded lengths. Allocations are unchecked; backward filling is a presentation choice rather than proof of better performance.
evidence_basis: Static comparison of two equally linear formatting implementations; no timing benchmark.
